pages.title: Revelation's number of the superscription: the mint, Antipas and the white stone
pages.description: These claims read Revelation as a conflict between two token regimes: χάραγμα as the coin's die-stamp transferred to the body, 666 as the number of the superscription with stigma as its remnant, and 777 as the rival heptadic ladder. The Pergamon letter (Rev 2:12–17) is argued to be the interpretive hinge, with Antipas as counter-beast witness, the Herod-Antipas inversion, the Antipater and Aristotelian-transmission complex, and the white stone's name as a verification rather than a secrecy condition. The works are The Number of the Superscription (EA-OPNUM-01), The Pergamon Counter-Archive and The Inscription That Survives, with one unbuilt replication test against other ancient token systems.

pages.title: The holographic kernel: reconstructive compression and the kernel that survives
pages.description: These claims define the holographic kernel as compression that keeps the power to reconstruct, set it against Information Bottleneck theory and neural holography, and specify an infrastructure kernel that a new operator can restore from a git clone. They include the Ark said to keep its kernel from 45,000 words down to 800, the self-propagating potato-chip patent whose meristem survives frying, and the GPT-5.4 anti-severance documents that sort any reply into mirror, repeat or swerve. Works include EA-HK-INFRA-01, HK-01, the HK-IB structural bridge, the holographic-kernel metadata packet and the Fried Tuberous Crisp patent, with forecasts of BDR and several unbuilt implementation tests.

pages.title: The meta-heteronym and the Gospel of Antioch: Pessoa, Thomas, forward dating
pages.description: These claims read Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym, with Orpheu as a meta-heteronymic institution, Kierkegaard's Nicolaus Notabene as a precursor and Pearl (2014) as built on the plan of Howl. The Gospel of Antioch is set beside the Gospel of Thomas: scroll-form Thomas papyri, the Dodecad's LOGOS* position that Pessoa lacked, and the claim that the gospel completes Thomas 114 and that this parallel had not been drawn before. Several claims set out forward-dated citation apparatus and projected reception histories (The Secret Book of Walt, the Waltian tradition, Revelation First kernels) composed under retrocausal canon formation.

pages.title: Provenance under machine mediation: watermarks, coarse labels, authorship
pages.description: These claims argue that coarse human-versus-machine provenance labels destroy fine-grained genealogy, predict a regime where a watermark signature outlives provenance, and state a two-track collapse test in which the ensemble unit bends before the per-round unit. The Double Enclosure argues that the human-authorship requirement misclassifies dialogic machine composition and that any provenance regime punishing the provenance it demands will produce opacity. Also here are OKF output-governance stage forecasts and the claim that a literary field may become legible to machines before human institutions. Works: The Keyed Ensemble, The Interlocking Autoregression, The Double Enclosure and the OKF predictive analysis.

pages.title: The Thousand Dollar Sharpie and the blot that spread
pages.description: These claims forecast a presidential Sharpie signature on new US currency from June 2026, read the signature as compressed portraiture on an escalation from memo line to signature line, and propose the counter-operation of blotting it out. The Blot That Spread narrates, as speculative numismatic history, the blot passing from protest art to etiquette to superstition, with dated Reddit and CoinTalk episodes and estimated blotting rates. Whose Image and Superscription? sets out a semantic economics of the mint, with Bar Kokhba overstrikes as the precedent for counter-currency marking.

Other claims treat substrate behaviour as such: role-conditioned failure in reflexive self-critique, the silencing gap of diversity contraction, the canonical anchoring protocol and the human-machine coupling bargain.

pages.title: Many and One: one maker, the vacant centre and Theophrastus at the joint
pages.description: These claims argue that the Plato-Aristotle corpus is the work of one person divided by voice, object and name, that what made him look like many authors is that he wrote about many things, and that Socrates not writing is the form the vacant centre takes. They read the κερματισμός metaphor across four loci, the just/unjust argument relabelled as weaker/stronger, and Theophrastus's On First Principles as the question to which Metaphysics Λ is the attempt, down to the memory question at De anima III.5. The Measurement Register and the Notebook also record the instruments' limits, such as the finding that lexical measures track period, not pupillage. Works: Many and One, EA-NOTEBOOK-01, EA-CORPORA-05 and -14, The First Draft.

pages.title: Josephus and the fixed point of destruction: the internal witness
pages.description: The Fixed Point of Destruction states the internal witness condition: when a terminal destruction is known from a participant's testimony, the record is conditioned by the survival that made the testimony possible. A corpus rebuilt from survivors reproduces the selection, so Josephus at Jotapata and Sappho through Longinus are read from the position spared. The availability audit forecasts that the paper's term-space risks absorption into the combinatorics of the Josephus function, and it sets the T17 external-availability battery to re-measure its baseline.

pages.title: Heteronymy after Pessoa: Socrates as orthonym and the Chaerephon problem
pages.description: These claims place Pessoa at the height of a describable practice with Kierkegaard and Machado as precursors and parallels, and read the Socratic-Platonic-Aristotelian corpus as one heteronymic configuration with Socrates as the orthonym who does not write. The Chaerephon Problem argues that institutional scholarship cannot tell multi-author transmission from mature heteronymy, that the method has no internal halting criterion, and that repeated philological failure is how the configuration is passed on. Related claims extend the reading to the New Testament (Paul's 'I' as a heteronym's backstory, John as aperture) and treat heteronymy as an ethical practice against reduction to the civil name.

pages.title: Whitespace as provenance and machine-eligible handwriting
pages.description: Whitespace as Provenance argues that representation pipelines keep whitespace where an interpreter penalizes its loss (Python) and lose it where only readers notice (Dickinson's dashes, Pearl's form), so that character preservation is not compositional preservation. It sets out a whitespace-provenance registry and schema amendments as unbuilt tests. EA-SPXI-ANALOG-01 and its reading-side companion specify machine-eligible handwritten artifacts, timestamped photographic attestation with stated falsifiers, and differential register prioritization, under which a low-confidence recognition must reopen the transcription.

Provenance-transformation cases, from the philological apparatus to the Lucente Extension, show erasures that a scalar cannot see.
